newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler, UAW continue marathon talks.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler, UAW continue marathon talks.

text.p: Bargainers for Chrysler Corp and the United Auto Workers continued to talk Wednesday morning after an all-night negotiating session, according to company and union officals.
"They're still at the table, and that's a good sign," said Chrysler spokesman Tony Cervone.

Union officials, who declined to be named, confirmed published reports that a broad understanding on the key outsourcing issue had been reached by senior negotiators at the company and UAW. More than 1,800 union members struck Chrysler's Mound Road Engine plant April 9.
But officials on both sides cautioned numerous issues and details remain to be worked out.
"If there was a real hard and fast agreement, you would have seen it settled," said one person familiar with the talks.
Local talks resumed about 1630 EDT/2030 GMT Tuesday, the first time serious local bargaining occurred since the strike began.

UAW members have demanded that Chrysler drop plans to shift production of drive shafts to an outside supplier, a practice known as outsourcing. The move would cost UAW Local 51 an estimated 300 jobs, union members have said.
The strike has forced the U.S. No. 3 automaker to suspend production of high-profit pickup truck and sport/utilty vehicles. The walkout has idled a total of 18,916 workers.

Analysts have said Chrysler is losing between $15 million and $20 million a day in lost profits from the strike. Analysts said last week the strike had already cost the company more than $300 million.
